title: Twists preserve finiteness conditions
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, an integer $n\geq1$, and a scheme $S$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Use the twists $\Lambda(m)$ and $K(m)$ of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], for $m\in\mathbf Z$ and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$.

At finite coefficients, $A_{E,n}(m)$ is an invertible locally constant rank-one sheaf of $(A_{E,n})_S$-modules. At integral coefficients, $\mathcal O_E(m)$ is an invertible locally free rank-one module over the completed coefficient sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,S}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], with finite-level reductions $A_{E,j}(m)$ for every $j\geq1$. Here invertible means that tensoring with its sheaf dual gives the coefficient sheaf; locally free of rank one means isomorphic to that coefficient sheaf on a covering of the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. At $E$ and $\Qlb$, invertibility means invertibility of the images of these lines in the rationalized category [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and its common-finite-stage coefficient category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], respectively.

For every displayed coefficient, twisting preserves $D^b_c(S,\Lambda)$ and $D^b_{ctf}(S,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. At finite coefficients it preserves the cohomological vanishing interval and every Tor-amplitude interval $[a,b]$. At integral coefficients it preserves the single cohomological interval and the single Tor-amplitude interval valid for all derived reductions, and preserves derived completeness. The inverse twist is $(-)(-m)$. The $E$ and $\Qlb$ assertions are interpreted on integral representatives and at common finite stages, as in the coefficient definitions; no ambient category of arbitrary discrete $E$- or $\Qlb$-module sheaves is asserted.

proof.text: Let $R$ be $(A_{E,n})_S$ or $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,S}$. The finite and integral assertions of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free], clauses 3 and 4, give a covering on which $\Lambda(1)$ is $R$, its finite reductions, and the integral membership of $\mathcal O_E(1)$ in $D^b_c$. Apply the tensor-power and sheaf-Hom definitions of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. On the same covering every positive power is $R^{\otimes m}\cong R$, and its dual is $\mathcal Hom_R(R,R)\cong R$. Thus $L=\Lambda(m)$ is locally free of rank one for every integer $m$, including $m=0$ and $m<0$. The evaluation maps $L\otimes_R L^\vee\to R$ and $L^\vee\otimes_R L\to R$ are isomorphisms: locally they are multiplication $R\otimes_R R\to R$. These maps are defined without a choice of basis, so the local inverses agree on overlaps and glue. The tensor and Hom formulas identify $L^\vee$ with $\Lambda(-m)$ for $m\geq0$; for $m<0$ use the canonical bidual map from the positive power to its double dual, which locally is $R\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(\operatorname{Hom}_R(R,R),R)$, an isomorphism by evaluation at $1$. This uses the completed sheaf as integral unit, not the discrete constant sheaf $(\mathcal O_E)_S$.

source.place: Proof, first sentence and the tensor-power/internal-Hom sentence; the rank-one input is the existing coefficient-construction lemma (Stacks 03PK, 040M, 03RV for its finite-level part).

proof.text: For either $R$ from step 1, put $T_L(F)=F\otimes_R L$. Associativity, symmetry and unit maps of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], followed by the evaluation isomorphisms in step 1, give $T_{L^\vee}T_L(F)\cong F$ and $T_LT_{L^\vee}(F)\cong F$, naturally in $F$. Hence these are inverse additive equivalences. They preserve kernels and cokernels directly by their universal properties: for example maps $B\to T_L(\ker f)$ correspond, after applying $T_{L^\vee}$, to maps $T_{L^\vee}B\to\ker f$, hence exactly to maps $B\to T_L(\operatorname{dom}f)$ killed by $T_L(f)$; for cokernels, maps $T_L(\operatorname{coker}f)\to B$ correspond to maps $\operatorname{coker}f\to T_{L^\vee}B$, hence exactly to maps $T_L(\operatorname{cod}f)\to B$ annihilating $T_L(f)$. Thus $T_L$ is exact, so $L$ is flat by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: invertibility and flatness; elementary universal-property verification of exactness.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] and [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] to the exact functors $T_L$ and $T_{L^\vee}$ from step 2. They act termwise on complexes, induce inverse triangulated equivalences, and satisfy $\mathcal H^i(T_L C)\cong\mathcal H^i(C)\otimes_R L$ for every complex, without a boundedness assumption. To identify this functor with derived tensor, first observe that $L[0]$ and $L^\vee[0]$ are K-flat with flat terms: tensoring any acyclic complex with either is exactly its termwise image under the corresponding exact functor, hence remains acyclic by the cohomology formula. Choose $P\to C$ K-flat with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Exactness makes $P\otimes_RL\to C\otimes_RL$ a quasi-isomorphism. The terms of $P\otimes_RL$ are flat: tensor with $P^i\otimes_RL$ is the composite of the exact functors tensor with $P^i$ and $T_L$. Moreover $P\otimes_RL$ is K-flat: for any acyclic $B$, the total complex $B\otimes_R(P\otimes_RL)$ identifies, by termwise tensor associativity, with $(B\otimes_RP)\otimes_RL$, which is acyclic since $P$ is K-flat and $T_L$ is exact. In this rebracketing, $T_L$ commutes with the direct sums in the total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], since the closed tensor statement makes it a left adjoint: $\operatorname{Hom}(T_L(\bigoplus_i B_i),D)\cong\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(T_LB_i,D)$. The degree-zero line introduces no additional differential sign. The derived tensor computation of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] applies to the two K-flat flat-term complexes $P$ and $L[0]$ and gives $C\otimes_R^LL\cong T_L(C)$. In particular the cohomology formula holds for derived tensor. Both $L$ and its dual have amplitude $[0,0]$, and the inverse equivalence shows that $\mathcal H^i(C\otimes_R^LL)$ vanishes exactly when $\mathcal H^i(C)$ vanishes.

source.place: Proof, cohomology formula: replace the unprovided spectral sequence by exact tensor on complexes (Stacks 010N, 015F, 06YS, 03EO).

proof.text: Take $R=(A_{E,n})_S$ and $C\in D^b_c(S,A_{E,n})$. For each nonzero $\mathcal H^i(C)$ choose its finite constructible stratification as in [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. On a stratum, the restriction of $\mathcal H^i(C)\otimes_RL$ is the tensor of the restrictions, by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] applied to the immersion of that stratum, with its pro-etale module pullback [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Pulling back the trivializing cover of $L$ gives a cover of the stratum and identifies the pulled-back line there with the constant rank-one module. Refine the local trivializing covers of this locally constant sheaf and of the rank-one line $L$ by their fibre products over the stratum. On each resulting object the tensor is $M\otimes_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,n}\cong M$, with $M$ the original finite module. Thus the same finite partition still proves constructibility, and its stalks remain finite; no finite trivializing cover of the entire scheme is needed. Step 3 preserves the cohomological vanishing interval. This proves finite-level bounded constructibility, for $L$ and its dual.

source.place: Proof, preservation of finite partitions and locally constant finite stalks, with the inverse-image tensor comparison made explicit (Stacks 03EL).

proof.text: Still at finite coefficients, suppose $C$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. For an arbitrary sheaf $M$ placed in degree zero, choose also a K-flat flat-term resolution $Q\to M$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], and use the K-flat $P$ of step 3. Since $P\otimes_RL$ is K-flat, $(C\otimes_R^LL)\otimes_R^LM$ is represented by $(P\otimes_RL)\otimes_RQ\cong(P\otimes_RQ)\otimes_RL$, by the total-tensor direct-sum comparison proved in step 3 and the sheaf tensor symmetry and associativity of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. The latter is $T_L$ applied to the representative of $C\otimes_R^LM$. Exactness and the cohomology formula of step 3 imply that its cohomology vanishes outside $[a,b]$. The implication just proved also holds with $L^\vee$ as its line; applying that implication to $C\otimes_R^LL$ and using $(C\otimes_R^LL)\otimes_R^LL^\vee\cong C$ proves the converse. Thus the entire Tor interval, rather than merely existence of some finite interval, is preserved. This tests all module sheaves $M$, not just constructible ones.

source.place: Proof, preservation of the vanishing interval in the finite Tor-amplitude condition; explicit K-flat rebracketing.

proof.text:
For the integral stage write $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,S}$, $A_j=(A_{E,j})_S$, and $L=\mathcal O_E(m)$. Reducing a trivialization $L|_V\cong R|_V$ gives $L_j=L\otimes_RA_j$ free of rank one locally. The canonical base-change maps for tensor powers and their duals are isomorphisms, since locally they are the identities on $A_j$; hence step 1 and [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] identify $L_j$ with $A_{E,j}(m)$ for every $j$. Choose $P\to C$ as in step 3. The termwise rebracketing map
$$(P\otimes_RL)\otimes_RA_j\cong(P\otimes_RA_j)\otimes_{A_j}L_j$$
is an isomorphism of complexes. The left computes the reduction of $C\otimes_R^LL$, by [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], because $P\otimes_RL$ is K-flat with flat terms; on the right $P\otimes_RA_j$ is K-flat over $A_j$ by [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings]. Also $L_j[0]$ is K-flat with flat terms by the finite-level calculation of step 3, so the two-input derived tensor formula applies on the right. Thus
$$(C\otimes_R^LL)\otimes_R^LA_j\cong (C\otimes_R^LA_j)\otimes_{A_j}^LA_{E,j}(m).$$
These maps are compatible with $A_{j+1}\to A_j$ and the maps from $C$: on tensor representatives they send $(x\otimes l)\otimes a$ to $(x\otimes a)\otimes(l\otimes1)$; reducing either before or after this formula has the same result. After restriction of scalars, the same comparison for a reduction complex $B$ is the termwise identity $B\otimes_RL\cong B\otimes_{A_j}L_j$; it computes $T_L$ on that reduction since $T_L$ is exact, without assuming $B$ is K-flat over $R$. The tensor computations use the ringed-site derived tensor of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], so no discrete integral coefficient category is substituted.

source.place: Proof, final sentence: make the levelwise integral reduction formula and its transition compatibility explicit; ringed-site K-flat change of rings (Stacks 06YS and the cited change-of-rings node).

proof.text:
The integral derived equivalences $T_L$ and $T_{L^\vee}$ of step 3 preserve the countable products that occur in [def-weil-derived-complete]. Indeed for every derived object $B$ and family $(C_j)$ there are natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(B,T_L(\prod_jC_j))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(T_{L^\vee}B,\prod_jC_j)\cong\prod_j\operatorname{Hom}(T_{L^\vee}B,C_j)\cong\prod_j\operatorname{Hom}(B,T_LC_j).$$
This is exactly the product universal property; it identifies the comparison with the map having components $T_L$ of the projections. The following argument is quantified over either line from step 1. Let $C$ be derived complete. Apply the triangulated functor from [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] to its defining distinguished Roos triangle
$$C\xrightarrow{c}\prod_jC_j\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_jC_j\longrightarrow C[1],$$
where $C_j$ denotes its derived reduction restricted back to $R$-modules. The product isomorphisms and step 6 identify this triangle with a Roos triangle for the reductions of $T_LC$. Its first map has the reduction maps as components, and its second map is $1-s$ for that tower, by the compatibility checked in step 6. Consequently $T_LC$ is derived complete by precisely the existential Roos-triangle condition of [def-weil-derived-complete]. This does not choose a purported unique morphism into a derived limit. Taking the line in this quantified argument to be $L^\vee$ proves preservation by the inverse twist.

source.place: Proof, final sentence: supply the derived-completeness argument, using the existing definition and exact-functor theorem (Stacks 015F); product preservation is proved by its universal property, not inferred merely from triangulatedness.

proof.text: For integral $C\in D^b_c(S,\mathcal O_E)$, [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] gives derived completeness and one cohomological interval $[r,s]$ for all its reductions. Steps 4 and 6 give bounded constructible reductions of $T_LC$, and step 3 gives the very same interval $[r,s]$ independently of $j$; step 7 gives completeness. This is exactly membership in the integral $D^b_c$. If $C$ satisfies the integral finite-Tor condition, its reductions have one Tor interval $[a,b]$ independent of $j$ by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]; steps 5 and 6 preserve that same interval. All statements hold for the inverse line as well. In particular applying this argument to the integral unit, or applying step 7 to the complete rank-one line already supplied in step 1 and its powers and duals, shows that every $\mathcal O_E(m)$ belongs to the integral category. To see the unit directly, the integral line $\mathcal O_E(1)$ is complete by step 1 and its tensor with the inverse line is the unit; step 7 preserves completeness, and its reductions are $A_{E,j}$ in degree zero.

source.place: Proof, final sentence: check uniform integral cohomological and Tor bounds, including the integral unit and negative powers.

proof.text:
The integral functors $T_L,T_{L^\vee}$ are $\mathcal O_E$-linear, as is visible from tensoring maps. In [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] they therefore induce inverse functors on $D^b_c(S,E)$: objects go to $T_L(C)$ and a localized morphism $f\otimes a$ goes to $T_L(f)\otimes a$. The inverse identities of step 2 remain identities after localization, so the images $E(m)$ are invertible. For $E\subset F$, write $R_E=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,S}$ and $R_F=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,S}$, and let $\operatorname{Ext}_{F/E}$ be the completed integral scalar extension underlying [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. By [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], its natural comparison from ordinary change of rings is an isomorphism on every complete object. Steps 7-8 therefore allow this comparison both for $C$ and for $C(m)$. For the first line, put $R_0=\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,S}$ and $T=\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_S$. Clause 3 of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free], applied to each of $E$ and $F$, identifies $R_0\otimes_{(\mathbf Z_\ell)_S}(\mathcal O_H)_S$ with $R_H$ for $H=E,F$. Combining these identifications with the defining formula $\mathcal O_H(1)=T\otimes_{(\mathbf Z_\ell)_S}(\mathcal O_H)_S$ gives $\mathcal O_H(1)\cong T\otimes_{R_0}R_H$. Tensor associativity therefore gives the natural line isomorphism
$$\mathcal O_E(1)\otimes_{R_E}R_F\cong(T\otimes_{R_0}R_E)\otimes_{R_E}R_F\cong T\otimes_{R_0}R_F\cong\mathcal O_F(1).$$
For positive powers tensor associativity extends it to the corresponding powers; for negative powers the base-change map on sheaf duals is locally $\operatorname{Hom}_{R_E}(R_E,R_E)\otimes_{R_E}R_F\to\operatorname{Hom}_{R_F}(R_F,R_F)$, the identity on $R_F$, and hence is an isomorphism globally. This gives $\mathcal O_E(m)\otimes_{R_E}R_F\cong\mathcal O_F(m)$ for every $m$. On a K-flat flat-term representative $P\to C$, the resulting tensor comparison is the chain isomorphism
$$(P\otimes_{R_E}\mathcal O_E(m))\otimes_{R_E}R_F\cong(P\otimes_{R_E}R_F)\otimes_{R_F}\mathcal O_F(m),$$
which sends $(x\otimes l)\otimes b$ to $(x\otimes b)\otimes(l\otimes1)$. Change of rings preserves K-flatness and flat terms by [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], so this computes ordinary derived change of rings. Composing with the natural scalar-comparison isomorphisms gives $\operatorname{Ext}_{F/E}(C(m))\cong\operatorname{Ext}_{F/E}(C)(m)$, naturally in $C$. For $E\subset F\subset G$, applying the displayed formula successively sends $(x\otimes l)\otimes b\otimes c$ to $(x\otimes bc)\otimes(l\otimes1)$, equal to the direct comparison; the line comparison has the same property because the displayed $T\otimes_{R_0}R_H$ description and its tensor/dual powers all use the associative multiplication maps on scalars. The completed-to-ordinary comparison is induced by the quotient maps with zero shifted-product component as stated in the finite-free comparison node; its naturality and these tensor formulas consequently identify the successive comparisons with the common-stage scalar-composition identifications. No choice of an isomorphism between unmarked Roos triangles is used here. Consequently a common-stage morphism $[F,f]$ in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] can be twisted by $[F,T_L(f)]$, using the displayed comparisons to identify its domain and codomain with the extensions of the twisted objects; replacing it by its image at a larger finite field gives the same class. This defines inverse twists on the common-stage category and invertibility of $\Qlb(m)$. At either field coefficient $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], so this also proves the field finite-Tor assertions. No passage from a finite-stage category to an unstated ambient discrete-sheaf category is used.

source.place: Proof, last sentence: integral representatives, rationalization and common finite stages; natural finite-free completed-scalar comparison and explicit ordinary tensor base change replace a comparison inferred only from Roos triangles.

split_report.summary: Split into nine explicit steps with no new nodes. Reused the existing first-twist rank-one lemma, exact-functor Mathlib leaves and ringed-site tensor tools. Distinguished the completed integral coefficient sheaf and finite-stage rational categories from discrete constant sheaves; checked all integer powers, arbitrary Tor test sheaves, compatible reductions, countable products, the defining Roos map and uniform bounds. STATEMENT-DISPUTED: the original unrestricted locally constant sheaf wording is not the integral/rational convention; the statement now spells out the coefficient-dependent meaning faithful to the revised coefficient definition. Second reading: supplied the flat-term K-flat hypotheses of tensor descent, resolved arbitrary Tor test sheaves in both-input computations, cited the integral reduction construction, and replaced the completed-tensor shortcut by the existing natural finite-free scalar comparison and explicit coherent tensor maps.
split_report.blueprint: The first two sentences of the blueprint proof are steps 1-2; its derived-tensor/cohomology sentence is step 3; finite constructibility and Tor are steps 4-5; the final integral/common-stage sentence is steps 6-9. The unit exceptional-adjoint route is unchanged.
